16. Credit Bureau and Repayment-History Rules

Condition Interpretation Action
Bureau score >= 700 Acceptable bureau profile Continue
Bureau score 650-699 Borderline profile Manual review
Bureau score 600-649 Weak profile Manual review only with strong mitigants
Bureau score < 600 Outside demo risk appetite Decline unless score is unavailable due to a
verified thin file
No bureau score / thin file Insufficient conventional history Manual review using income and banking
evidence
-Any 30+ days-past-due event in the previous 6 months triggers manual review.
-Any 60+ days-past-due event in the previous 12 months triggers decline.
-An active NPA, fraud flag, write-off or settled account reported in the previous 24 months triggers decline.
-More than five hard bureau enquiries in the previous 6 months triggers manual review.
-A clean repayment history may be treated as a mitigating factor but does not override a hard decline rule.

policy_evidence.text:
18. Decision Outcomes and Manual-Review Triggers

Recommendation Minimum conditions
Eligible for straight-through processing Low model risk; no hard decline or manual-review trigger;
Recommendation Minimum conditions
documents complete; affordability within standard limits.
Conditional approval Low or medium risk with a remediable condition such as reduced
amount, additional proof or guarantor.
Manual review Any medium/high model band, thin file, borderline affordability,
income discrepancy, recent enquiry spike, missing non-critical
document or conflicting data.
Decline At least one hard decline condition in Section 19.
18.1 Mandatory manual-review triggers include:
-Medium or high model-risk band.
-FOIR above 40% and up to 50%, or credit-to-income ratio above 3.0x and up to 5.0x.
-Bureau score below 700 but not subject to a hard decline.
-No bureau score or limited credit history.
-Declared-versus-observed income discrepancy of 10%-25%.
-Income volatility above 30% across the available observation period.
-Requested amount within 10% of a product or exposure cap.
-Student applicant or any application requiring a guarantor.
-Conflicting KYC, employment, account-ownership or repayment information that can potentially be resolved.

policy_evidence.text:
15. Affordability and Exposure Limits

15.1 Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio (FOIR). For the demo, FOIR is calculated as existing monthly debt
obligations plus the proposed EMI, divided by verified net monthly income.
Threshold Interpretation Action
FOIR <= 40% Within standard affordability range Continue to remaining rules
FOIR > 40% and <= 50% Elevated repayment burden Manual review or lower sanctioned
amount
FOIR > 50% Unacceptable repayment burden Decline
15.2 Credit-to-income ratio. Requested credit divided by verified annual income is assessed as follows:
Credit / annual income Interpretation Action
<= 3.0x Standard range Continue
Credit / annual income Interpretation Action
> 3.0x and <= 5.0x High leverage Manual review or reduced amount
> 5.0x Outside demo risk appetite Decline
-The maximum sanctioned amount is the lower of the applicable product cap, five times verified annual income and
the amount supported by the FOIR test.
-A request within 10% of any maximum limit is routed to manual review.
-The applicant should retain a positive residual monthly income after all obligations; negative or near-zero residual
income is a decline condition.

policy_evidence.text:
19. Automatic Decline Conditions

Human-control requirement
A hard-rule decline may be automatically recommended, but the API or LLM must not execute a legal sanction decision.
The reason and supporting evidence must be available for authorized review.
-KYC or identity verification failure, invalid consent, confirmed fraud match or prohibited customer/use case.
-No verifiable regular income for an unsecured loan, except an eligible student case with an acceptable guarantor.
-FOIR above 50% or credit-to-annual-income ratio above 5.0x.
-Active NPA, confirmed fraud, write-off or settled credit account within the previous 24 months.
-Any 60+ days-past-due event within the previous 12 months.
-Bureau score below 600 when the score is valid and adverse repayment history is also present.
-Age outside the product eligibility range at maturity.
-Material document manipulation, unexplained income discrepancy above 25%, or a negative residual-income
assessment.
